items.hook: Frank Eugene Corder fatally crashes a single-engine Cessna 150 into the White House's south lawn, striking the West Wing. There were no other casualties.
items.body: Frank Eugene Corder was an American truck driver. The world is stranger than it lets on.

items.hook: Five minutes to steal a Renoir: Why museum thefts are becoming bolder across Europe
items.body: Art crime investigators and security experts say burglaries from galleries across Europe are becoming more brazen.

items.hook: Naomi Klein: ‘Extreme wealth has a deranging effect. It turns you into a supremacist’
items.body:
She’s tackled neoliberalism and the digital world, now the writer and activist is taking on tech billionaires. She explains how the super-rich are capitalising on climate and financial chaos in pursuit of power

Naomi Klein

items.hook: Leó Szilárd, waiting for a red light on Southampton Row in Bloomsbury, conceives the idea of the nuclear chain reaction.
items.body: Leo Szilard was a Hungarian-born American physicist, biologist and inventor who made numerous important discoveries in nuclear physics and the biological sciences. Bring it up somewhere. Watch the reaction.

items.hook: Bonanza, the first regularly scheduled TV program presented in color, is launched in the United States.
items.body: Bonanza is an American Western television series that ran on NBC from September 12, 1959, to January 16, 1973. One of those things you can't un-know.

items.hook: How a BBC strike exterminated Doctor Who adventure
items.body: Marcus Hearn recalls the stories his father told him about the filming of episodes in Cambridge.
